t: This is the place associated with Living Streets, the UK charity for everyday walking. Its goal is to promote pedestrian safety. It was founded in 1929 as the Pedestrians' Association, became the Pedestrians' Association for Road Safety in 1952, and took its current name in 2001. The founder was Robert Cecil, a lawyer, politician and diplomat. He was one of the architects of the League of Nations and a defender of it, and his service to that organisation won him the Nobel Peace Prize in 1937. Living Streets is a voting member of the International Federation of Pedestrians.
